kitty_graphics.value: none today. vte 0.15 (under alacritty_terminal 0.26) sends ESC _ (APC), ESC ^ (PM) and ESC X (SOS) into State::SosPmApcString, whose bytes go to anywhere(), which reacts only to CAN, SUB and ESC; the Perform trait has no APC method, so every Kitty graphics command is discarded before alacritty sees it. Under this option TD would write the whole protocol itself in its read loop — not started.

pub struct Grid<T> {" — [measured] `pub struct Term<T> {` at term/mod.rs:268 has no such derive. Under this option a snapshot must also re-send images still referenced by placeholder cells — [inferred].

threading_and_loop.value: By default the library owns the loop: EventLoop::spawn starts a "PTY reader" thread that owns the PTY, takes a lease plus an unfair lock on Arc<FairMutex<Term>> and calls Processor::advance on up to 1 MiB at a time. It includes a PTY layer (tty::Pty over rustix-openpty; ConPTY on Windows). Under this option the embedder owns the loop: Term is a plain struct with no internal locking, Processor::advance(&mut term, bytes) is public, and TD must flush a pending synchronized update (Processor::stop_sync / sync_bytes_count, both public) before acting on a graphics command.
threading_and_loop.note: quote: "state.parser.advance(&mut **terminal, &buf[..unprocessed]);" — [measured] thread name at event_loop.rs:206, lease at :117 and unfair lock at :140-142, READ_BUFFER_SIZE 0x10_0000 at :24; stop_sync / sync_bytes_count at vte ansi.rs:315,362.

reply_channel.value: Replies are events, not writes: Term calls EventListener::send_event(Event::PtyWrite(String)) for DA, DSR and mode reports, and TextAreaSizeRequest / ColorRequest / ClipboardLoad carry formatter closures. Nothing in the library writes them to the PTY; the embedder does, which is how TD answers exactly once in the host (host.rs:744) while the window replica swallows PtyWrite and TextAreaSizeRequest (term.rs:95-101). Kitty a=q replies would be written by TD's own loop, since vte never sees the query.
reply_channel.note:
quote: "/// Write some text to the PTY.
    PtyWrite(String)," — [measured] DA1 path at term/mod.rs:1261-1262; EventListener::send_event at event.rs:103-104.

td_migration.value: host.rs: replace EventLoop::new(…).spawn() (host.rs:726-729) with a TD reader per pane that splits the stream at Kitty APC terminators, advances the Processor for the bytes before each, then handles the command with &mut Term; re-prove the attach fence (host.rs:18-29), which today relies on alacritty's lease discipline; the TeeReader (host.rs:134-180) becomes a step inside TD's loop. socketpty.rs: shrinks to a socket read in TD's loop, and the two hand-copied pub(crate) poll tokens (:40-50) go away. term.rs: window-owned panes move from EventLoop/Notifier to the same loop; the PtyWrite bounce and the replica's reply filter stay. gridwire.rs: grid encoding and grid_hash unchanged; add re-sending referenced images on attach. pane.rs: the 51 grid reads stay; the renderer learns to draw U+10EEEE cells from an image store. main.rs, pane/bench.rs: no change (they only use WindowSize, tty::setup_env, TermMode). No fork.
td_migration.note: [inferred] from TD's files on research/terminal-core @426f072 and alacritty_terminal 0.26's public API (grid_mut, Handler for Term, Processor::advance/stop_sync all public). Effort L. host.rs already answers CSI 16 t from the tee (host.rs:747-749), so a scanner seat exists.

biggest_risk.value: Owning the loop means re-proving, against code TD now owns, the one hard invariant of the host/window split — every byte lands on exactly one side of an attach snapshot — while a stream splitter that disagrees with vte about where a string ends (CAN/SUB, ESC inside OSC, buffered synchronized updates) corrupts panes without failing loudly.
biggest_risk.note: [inferred] the attach fence is documented as "the only hard part" in host.rs:12-29 and is written against alacritty's EventLoop.

td_migration.value: Cargo.toml: add [patch.crates-io] vte = TD's fork (PR #115's Perform callbacks plus forwarding through ansi::Processor to new ansi::Handler methods, which PR #115 does not do) and point alacritty_terminal at a TD fork whose Term holds an image store and implements those methods. host.rs, term.rs, socketpty.rs: unchanged — alacritty's EventLoop still drives parsing, so the attach fence and SocketPty survive. gridwire.rs: the snapshot must re-send images the host's Term holds (Kitty a=t ahead of the rows) and grid_hash must decide whether placements count. pane.rs: the 51 grid reads stay; the renderer reads placements from the patched Term and draws them. main.rs, pane/bench.rs: no change. Ongoing: rebase both forks on every alacritty_terminal release (2 stable in the last 12 months). A no-alacritty-fork variant — a TD Handler wrapper delegating all 71 ansi::Handler methods to Term — needs TD to call Processor::advance itself, which is the own-loop route's host.rs rewrite.

biggest_risk.value: TD becomes the permanent maintainer of two forks — a vte whose APC PR upstream closed for inactivity and whose maintainer has floated a rewrite, and an alacritty_terminal whose Term must be re-patched on every release — unless TD finishes PR #115 upstream itself.
biggest_risk.note: [inferred] upstream was not hostile: the maintainer reviewed PR #115 as "Honestly seems fine to me. Just some minor nits." (2025-03-12) before it lapsed; see bubble.

bubbles.note: vte's APC PR was not refused; it lapsed. The maintainer's last review of PR #115 (2025-03-12) reads "Honestly seems fine to me. Just some minor nits.", a benchmark PR (alacritty #8507) found "The perf looks pretty much the same", and the PR was closed on 2026-07-12 only with "Closing due to inactivity." Issue #109 is still open, where the maintainer wrote "That shouldn't be difficult to add tbh, it mainly doesn't exist yet because I've had no use for it so far." Finishing #115 upstream would turn the vte half of this option from a permanent fork into an ordinary crates.io upgrade; the 'second rate escape sequence' remark is a design reservation from 2024-10-16, not a refusal.
bubbles.why: Changes the patched-vte option's cost from 'carry a fork forever' to 'land one PR', and it softens the morning write-up's reading that upstream will not supply this.

bubbles.note: Warp carries a copy of PR #115 on vte 0.15.0: branch copied-apc-support-0.15.0 at warpdotdev/vte (d94bf79e, 2025-03-21), and a commenter (heysweet) wrote on #115 "We'd really like to support Kitty Image protocol in the Warp terminal, and this PR would help us get there" (2025-02-03). That is a second alacritty-lineage terminal taking this exact route.
bubbles.why: Prior art and a possible ally for landing the PR upstream.

bubbles.note: copa (Rio's published vte fork, crates.io, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 0.4.2 of 2026-05-03) already has apc_start/apc_put/apc_end on Perform with the same signatures as PR #115, but it ships no ansi module (src/ has definitions.rs, lib.rs, params.rs, table.rs), so it cannot stand in for vte under alacritty_terminal, which needs vte::ansi::{Processor, Handler}. crates.io also sorts a 2023 copa 0.12.0 as max_version above the current 0.4.x line.
bubbles.why: Answers 'is there a published APC-capable vte?': yes, but not a drop-in one.

bubbles.note: asyncritty (dfoxfranke, Apache-2.0, crates.io 0.1.0-alpha3, created 2026-09-05) replaces alacritty's EventLoop with Tokio: "It runs processes on pseudoterminals (PTYs), handles asynchronous input and output, and parses terminal output into Alacritty's terminal model". Its author also landed two alacritty_terminal commits in August 2026. It is a working example of an embedder owning the read loop around a stock alacritty_terminal.
bubbles.why: Prior art for the own-loop option's hardest part.

bubbles.note: alacritty master (after 0.26.0) now caps zero-width characters at 9 per cell (commit ede2ac14, 2026-08-26, "Fix unbounded zerowidth character limit": `const MAX_ZEROWIDTH_CHARS: usize = 9;`, storage changed from Vec to ArrayVec). Kitty placeholder cells need at most 3 diacritics, so the placeholder plan survives, but the morning write-up's "appends zero-width characters … without a cap" will be stale at the next release.
bubbles.why: Placeholder cells are the anchor both Kitty routes rely on; the next alacritty_terminal release touches that storage.

bubbles.note: TD's host already answers CSI 16 t from the tee: the comment at host.rs:747-749 begins "`CSI 14 t` from the parser and `CSI 16 t` from the tee," and says both are answered from the pane's current size; TeeReader::read (host.rs:154-180) replies before the parser sees the chunk. The morning write-up's "CSI 16 t … never answered" is stale on research/terminal-core @426f072, and a byte-scanner seat already exists in the host.
bubbles.why: Corrects an input fact other clusters may reuse.

bubbles.note: Several alacritty_terminal forks are published on crates.io under new names because git dependencies cannot be published: crow-alacritty-terminal ("published because git deps cannot ship via crates.io"), blit-alacritty-terminal and yas-alacritty-terminal (emoji-width fixes), cutty_terminal. A fork route is fine for AppImage/AUR builds, but if TD ever publishes a crate that depends on a forked core, it would have to publish the fork too.
bubbles.why: Distribution constraint for both fork options (patched-vte and graphics-fork).
